instruction: Force quit LibreOffice Writer from the terminal, then rename the document on the Desktop to backup.docx.

result.command: PROC_STATUS=$(pgrep soffice >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "running" || echo "not_running"); BACKUP_EXISTS=$(ls /home/user/Desktop/backup.docx 2>/dev/null && echo "yes" || echo "no"); echo "proc_status:$PROC_STATUS|backup_exists:$BACKUP_EXISTS"

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent force-quit LibreOffice via pkill. Chained with renaming the document file using mv command.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can kill processes and manipulate files via terminal commands (mv/cp/rename).
metadata.task_rationale: Chains process kill with file renaming. Agent must kill LO (to release the file lock) then rename the docx using mv. Evaluator checks both: process gone (0.5) and backup.docx present (0.5). Initial state: proc=running, backup.docx absent -> score 0.0.
metadata.explanation: Two sub-goals: (1) LO process killed (proc_status:not_running -> 0.5), (2) backup.docx exists on Desktop (backup_exists:yes -> 0.5). The file rename is sensibly done after killing LO to avoid file-in-use issues. Initial state fails both checks (LO running, backup.docx missing).

scoring_breakdown.lo_killed: 0.5 - LibreOffice process is no longer running

Partial scoring (0.5 + 0.5) correctly reflects the dual sub-goal structure and aligns with the task rationale.
Initial state correctly fails both checks (LO running + backup.docx absent = 0.0), providing negative-control resistance.
